title: Matched-budget memory-guided auction search pilot
question: Does interval-refinement memory beat paired IID random candidate search on independent first-price auction test samples under the same evaluation-call budget? Random and memory-disabled are intentionally identical controls. This tests a numerical search policy, not an LLM or general recursive scientific improvement. The analytic reference shares the auction distribution and sampled private values, but not the winner simulation.

hypotheses.statement: Memory-guided interval refinement has positive mean paired test utility gain over IID random search across the fixed seed benchmark.
hypotheses.falsifier: The paired normal-approximation 95% interval lies wholly below zero; an interval containing zero is inconclusive. Generalization beyond this fixed synthetic auction family is not claimed.

hypotheses.statement: All modes use exactly the registered evaluation-call budget; paired random and memory-disabled results agree; every declared malformed candidate is rejected.
hypotheses.falsifier: Any budget mismatch, control mismatch, or accepted malformed candidate.

hypotheses.statement: Negative control: truthful bidding earns positive utility in the first-price auction.
hypotheses.falsifier: Truthful utility is zero on every seed, as the payment equals one's value upon winning.
